inline_comments.comment: The r1/r2 non-intersection check has been semantically inverted. The original condition `r1 !== 0 && r2 !== 0 && sameSign(r1, r2)` correctly returns DON'T_INTERSECT when both endpoints of one segment are clearly on the same side of the other line (both non-zero, same sign). The replacement `Math.abs(r1) < epsilon && Math.abs(r2) < epsilon && sameSign(r1, r2)` only fires when both values are nearly zero — i.e., the near-collinear case, which is already handled by the `denom === 0` check further down. For the common non-intersection case (two segments clearly on the same side), this early return no longer triggers, so the function proceeds to compute and return a bogus intersection point. This will cause edges to connect at incorrect positions when drawing polygons (e.g. diamond/question shapes). The fix is to restore the original condition: `if (r1 !== 0 && r2 !== 0 && sameSign(r1, r2)) { return; }`.

`validateLayoutData` throws `'Root node is required'` when `data.rootNode` is absent. However, `cose-bilkent` is registered as a general layout loader in `render.ts` (via the `includeLargeFeatures` path), meaning any diagram type can opt into it with `layout: cose-bilkent`. Non-mindmap diagrams (flowcharts, sequence diagrams, etc.) will never have a `rootNode` in their `LayoutData`, so they will always throw here. Either remove the `rootNode` requirement from `validateLayoutData` for the shared layout system, or restrict cose-bilkent registration to mindmap-only usage.

`_drawNodes` is defined but never called anywhere in the new renderer. The new `draw` function delegates entirely to `render(data4Layout, svg)`. This is dead code and should be removed to avoid confusion about the intended rendering pipeline.

`_updateNodeDimensions` is defined but never called. It was apparently intended to update node dimensions in `data4Layout` after DOM insertion, but is not invoked anywhere in the file. This is dead code and should be removed. If node dimension updates are needed, the logic should be integrated into the `render` pipeline.

`detectType(text)` is newly added during preprocessing. If the diagram text is invalid or the diagram type is not yet registered (e.g., external diagram extensions loaded later), `detectType` will throw an exception. Previously, a syntactically bad diagram would fail gracefully at render time; now it fails hard during preprocessing. This is a potential regression for all diagram types, not just mindmaps. Consider wrapping in a try/catch and defaulting to a no-op if detection fails.

The edge is first removed via `data4Layout.edges.filter(...)`, which returns a new array without the item. The subsequent `findIndex` / `splice` on lines 131-134 is therefore dead code — `findIndex` will always return `-1` because the item was already removed by the filter. Remove the `findIndex`/`splice` block. Additionally, the filter callback reuses the name `edge`, shadowing the outer loop variable, which is error-prone.

`let intersectionShift = 50;` is initialized at the top of the function, but then unconditionally overwritten to `30` on line ~49 before any use. The initial value `50` is never read. Either initialize directly to `30` or make this a constant.

`const _edgeLabel = await insertEdgeLabel(edgeLabels, edge);` — the result is assigned but never used. The `_` prefix signals it's intentionally ignored, but `insertEdgeLabel` returns data needed to call `positionEdgeLabel`. Without using the return value, edge labels will not be positioned. Compare with how edge labels are handled in the ELK renderer.

A large block of `APA01`-prefixed debug log statements (spanning roughly lines 610–650) was added, including an O(n×m) validation loop that iterates all edges and all children just to emit log output. This logging should be removed or gated behind a debug flag before this merges to main. Production renders will perform unnecessary work on every layout call.

`(node?.padding || 0) * 1` is equivalent to `(node?.padding || 0)`. Multiplying by 1 is a no-op and reads as though a different multiplier was intended. The expression should be simplified to `node?.padding || 0`.

`shapeSvg.append(() => label.node())` moves the label — which was already inserted into `shapeSvg` by `labelHelper` — to the end of the container, so it renders above the background path and underline. This works, but differs from the pattern used by other shapes in this PR (`bang.ts`, `cloud.ts`) which instead insert the background at `:first-child`. Using the established `:first-child` insertion pattern for `bg` and `line` would be clearer and remove the need for the explicit re-append.

Double space in the test description: `'3-tidy-tree: should render a  mindmap with different shapes'` has two spaces before `mindmap`. Should be `'3-tidy-tree: should render a mindmap with different shapes'`.

`combineAndPositionTrees` accepts `_leftBoundingBox`, `_rightBoundingBox`, and `_data` parameters (all prefixed with `_`) which are unused. If these are placeholders for future use, document that intent. If they are not planned for use, remove them to keep the API surface clean.

The `node.from === 'mindmap'` condition couples a generic shape renderer to mindmap-specific logic. The same pattern appears in `drawRect.ts` and `squareRect.ts`. Mindmap-specific sizing behaviour should be expressed through the node's properties (e.g. existing `padding`, `width`, `height`) rather than by inspecting the originating diagram type inside a shared shape. This makes the shape harder to reuse and test independently.

Several `<pre>` blocks start with a leading space before `---` (e.g. ` ---` instead of `---`). YAML frontmatter delimiters are sensitive to leading whitespace; the indented `---` may not be recognized as a valid front-matter block by the mermaid parser, silently falling back to the default layout and giving misleading test baselines.

`diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now()` generates a non-deterministic ID on every call to `getData()`. This makes snapshot/visual tests unreliable (the diagram container's ID will differ between test runs) and prevents caching or deduplication based on diagram identity. A stable, deterministic identifier derived from the diagram content or a sequential counter would be more appropriate.

general_comments.comment: The `intersection` function (rectangle boundary intersection) in `packages/mermaid-layout-tidy-tree/src/layout.ts` is a near-verbatim copy of the code that was simultaneously deleted from `packages/mermaid-layout-elk/src/render.ts`. The same algorithm now lives in two separate packages with slightly different signatures. This logic should live in a shared utility (e.g. `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/intersect/`) so both layout packages can import it, rather than maintaining duplicate implementations.

The `mermaid-layout-tidy-tree` package's `package.json` has an empty `scripts` field (`{}`). Without build, test, lint, or typecheck scripts the package cannot be developed, verified, or published in isolation. At minimum, a `build` script that produces the `dist/` output referenced in `exports` and `module` should be provided, consistent with how `mermaid-layout-elk` is set up.

In `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/types.ts`, the `Edge` type gains `source` and `target` fields that are conceptually identical to the existing `start` and `end` fields. Having two pairs of names for the same relationship (from/to a node) will confuse contributors about which field to populate for new edge types. If `source`/`target` are needed for a specific layout algorithm's internal format, they should stay in that algorithm's local types rather than in the shared `Edge` interface.

Multiple elements in `cypress/platform/knsv2.html` use `id="diagram4"`, making several duplicate IDs in the same document. Duplicate IDs are invalid HTML and can cause unpredictable behaviour with `document.getElementById` and CSS selectors. Each diagram block should use a unique ID.
